headline: TERMITES?|SALE GUIDE
substantiveDifference: Explains four distinct termite documents: visible-evidence WDI report, treatment disclosure/scope, actual warranty terms and separate structural assessment. Current repair and disclosure pages do not explain these limits or the seller handoff.

faq.q: Does a clear WDI inspection guarantee there are no termites?
faq.a: No. The Texas Department of Agriculture explains that the inspection concerns visible evidence in readily accessible areas and is not a warranty that wood-destroying insects are absent.

faq.q: Is a termite inspection also a structural damage report?
faq.a: No. TDA explicitly distinguishes the WDI inspection from a structural damage report. Ask an appropriately qualified building professional about the extent and repair of suspected damage.

faq.q: Does a termite treatment invoice prove a warranty transfers?
faq.a: The invoice alone does not establish the warranty terms or transfer. Obtain the actual agreement and ask the issuing company to confirm coverage, renewal conditions and any ownership-change requirements in writing.

faq.q: Can I compare an as-is offer before repairing termite damage?
faq.a: You can ask Cash As-Is to evaluate the house in its current condition and explain what is known or still unresolved. Any proposal must be reviewed alongside applicable disclosure requirements, assessments and the actual agreement.
